before.title: Fuel Pump Mixing-Tube Burr Causing Engine Stall at Low Fuel (Recall 20V446 / GM N202314760)
before.description: Certain 2020 GMC Acadia vehicles (along with the Buick Enclave, Cadillac XT5/XT6 and Chevrolet Traverse) were built with a fuel pump assembly containing burrs inside the mixing tube. The burrs can prevent fuel transfer from the secondary to the primary side of the tank, so at low fuel levels the engine may not receive adequate fuel and can stall unexpectedly, increasing crash risk.
before.solution: NHTSA recall 20V446 (GM N202314760): dealers replace the fuel pump module free of charge. Owners can verify applicability by VIN at the NHTSA recall lookup and contact GMC customer service at 1-888-988-7267.
symptoms: Engine stalls unexpectedly, most likely when fuel level is low
Difficulty maintaining fuel supply as the tank nears empty
Possible difficulty restarting after a low-fuel stall

before.title: Incorrect Transmission Sun Gear Causing Driver-Side Half-Shaft Disengagement / Rollaway (Recall N222389310)
before.description: Approximately 7,800 GM crossovers including the 2023 GMC Acadia were built with an incorrectly machined transmission sun gear. The defect can cause the driver-side (left-front) half-shaft to disengage from the transmission, resulting in a sudden loss of drive power, or a vehicle rollaway when the transmission is placed in Park because the parking pawl can no longer hold the vehicle. Both outcomes raise crash risk.
before.solution: GM recall N222389310: dealers replace the sun gears free of charge. Owner notification letters were mailed July 27, 2023. Confirm by VIN at the NHTSA recall lookup and contact GMC at 1-800-462-8782; use the parking brake (don't rely on Park alone) until the repair is completed.
symptoms: Sudden loss of drive power / vehicle won't move
Clunk or disengagement felt from the driveline
Vehicle rolls away after being shifted to Park
Grinding or abnormal noise from the front transaxle

before.title: Infotainment System Lockup, Black Screen and Random Reboots (2nd-Gen IO/IOR Head Unit)
before.description: Second-generation GMC Acadias with the GM IO/IOR infotainment head unit suffer freezes, unresponsive touchscreens, sudden black screens and random reboots. When the unit locks up, owners lose the radio and hands-free calls, and the backup camera and on-screen controls can become unresponsive until the system reboots. It is a widely documented owner-reported pattern (with workarounds shared on owner forums); GM has separately faced infotainment class-action litigation, though that suit centers on the IOR display family rather than being an Acadia-specific recall.
before.solution: Try a global reset (turn the car off, open the driver door for ~3 minutes, then restart) or briefly disconnect the negative battery terminal for ~20 minutes; some owners trace it to a loose/fragile screen connector behind the glove box. Permanent fixes require a GM infotainment software update or head-unit replacement at a dealer per TSB. There is no recall for this issue.
symptoms: Hands-free calls drop and radio controls stop responding
Backup camera unavailable while the unit is frozen

citations.title: GM Bulletin 10217855 - Acadia Radio Resets or Reboots

proposal.title: Infotainment System Lockup, Black Screen and Random Reboots (2nd-Gen IO/IOR Head Unit)

before.title: Electric Power Steering (EPAS) Failure and Loss of Assist
before.description: The 2007-2016 Acadia uses an electric power steering rack that is prone to intermittent and permanent failure. The steering assist can fail suddenly with no warning, requiring significantly more physical effort to steer — a dangerous condition at highway speeds. NHTSA received over 800 complaints and opened an investigation. The failure mode involves the EPAS motor and control module overheating, producing a Service Power Steering warning. Failures are more common in warm climates and on vehicles that have been through multiple hot/cold cycles.
before.solution: EPAS rack replacement (GM 22873304 or ACDelco 84277937). EPAS module reprogram (resolves some intermittent failures). Ensure proper battery voltage — low battery causes false EPAS warnings. Dealer reprogram with latest software before condemning the rack.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power steering assist
Steering becomes very heavy especially at low speeds
Intermittent assist loss that returns on restart
Clunking from steering rack during turns
Steering wheel pulls to one side

citations.title: GM Bulletin 10248773 - Acadia Loss of Steering Assist

proposal.title: Electric Power Steering (EPAS) Failure and Loss of Assist

before.title: "Shift to Park" Message With No-Shutdown / Door-Lock Lockout and Battery Drain
before.description: Second-generation GMC Acadias (2017-2019) display a persistent "Shift to Park" message even when the shifter is fully in Park, due to a faulty shifter assembly / park-position microswitch that fails to confirm the Park signal. When triggered, the vehicle will not fully power down, the key/fob is retained, the doors will not lock, and the battery can drain overnight; owners often have to rock the shifter repeatedly to clear it. The fault is intermittent at first and worsens over time, and it prompted a GMC class-action lawsuit.
before.solution: GM addressed it through dealer repair (reseat/replace the console shifter assembly and park microswitch); a misaligned brake pedal position switch can produce the same message. Working the shifter through its full travel gives temporary relief, but a permanent fix requires the shifter/switch service. CarComplaints documents ~26 complaints on the 2018 model year with an average repair cost around $470.
symptoms: "Shift to Park" message displays while the transmission is in Park
Cannot turn the vehicle off or remove the key fob
Doors will not lock with the message active
Battery drains because the vehicle won't fully power down
Message appears and clears intermittently; must rock the shifter to clear it

before.title: Start/Stop Transmission Accumulator Missing Bolts - Fluid Leak, Loss of Propulsion and Fire Risk (Recall 20V668 / N202313440)
before.description: On 2019-2020 GMC Acadia models (part of a broader 2018-2020 GM crossover campaign) equipped with auto start/stop, the transmission accumulator endcap may have been assembled with missing or loose bolts. Because leaking transmission fluid near an ignition source can ignite, the defect also carries a fire risk.
before.solution: NHTSA recall 20V668 (GM N202313440): dealers inspect the start/stop transmission accumulator and replace it if any bolts are missing, free of charge. Verify by VIN at the NHTSA recall database.

Loss of propulsion / loss of drive power
Burning smell or fire risk from leaked fluid near hot components

before.title: 3.6L V6 Timing Chain Stretch and Premature Failure
before.description: The 3.6L LLT and LFX V6 engines in 2007-2016 Acadia are notorious for premature timing chain stretch and guide failure, typically between 60,000-120,000 miles. The engines use three separate timing chains (primary and two secondary), and all three are subject to premature stretch. Stretched chains cause cam timing correlation codes (P0008, P0009, P0016, P0017, P0018, P0019), rough running, and potential catastrophic engine damage if a chain jumps a tooth or breaks. Low oil level and using non-Dexos oil accelerates wear. GM issued TSB 09-06-01-008 acknowledging the issue.
before.solution: Replace all timing chains, guides, and tensioners as a complete set. Oil change with Dexos1 Gen 2 full synthetic every 5,000 miles is critical for prevention. GM extended warranty coverage on some VINs. Labor is 15-20 hours for LLT, 10-15 hours for LFX. Total job: $2,500-5,000.
symptoms: Check engine light with codes P0008, P0009, P0016, P0017, P0018, P0019
Rattling noise from front of engine on startup
Oil consumption (low oil accelerates chain wear)

citations.title: GM Bulletin 10245795 - High Feature V6 Timing-Chain Kits

proposal.title: 3.6L V6 Timing Chain Stretch and Premature Failure

proposal.solution: Complete the GM diagnostic procedure before ordering parts. When a stretched timing chain is confirmed, use the applicable GM timing-chain kit. before.title: 9T65 9-Speed Transmission Harsh Shifts and Hesitation
before.description: The second-generation Acadia (2017+) uses the GM 9T65 9-speed automatic transmission which shares known issues with the Chevrolet Traverse and Blazer. Common complaints include harsh 1-2 upshifts, hesitation between 5-15 mph, lurching on light throttle in stop-and-go traffic, and the transmission hunting between gears on hills. GM has released multiple TCM calibration updates. The transmission is extremely sensitive to fluid condition — extended intervals with aging Dexron HP fluid contribute significantly to shift quality degradation.
before.solution: TCM recalibration with latest software (multiple revisions released). Full transmission fluid exchange with Dexron HP (ACDelco/GM 19354121) every 45,000 miles. Valve body and solenoid pack replacement (OEM 24043134) if software updates fail. Allow 500+ miles for relearn after any TCM reset.
symptoms: Harsh or jerky 1-2 upshift between 5-15 mph
Hesitation when pulling away from a stop
Transmission hunting between gears on slight grades
Vibration or shudder during light acceleration
Delayed engagement from Park to Drive
Slip or flare on 2-3 shift under load

before.title: 3.6L V6 Internal Water Pump Failure and Coolant Leak
before.description: The 3.6L V6 engines (all generations) in the Acadia use a timing chain-driven internal water pump located inside the engine block rather than a traditional externally-driven pump. The internal water pump impeller is plastic and is prone to cracking or separating from the shaft between 80,000-140,000 miles. When the impeller fails, the engine loses coolant circulation leading to rapid overheating. Because the pump is internal, it is only accessible during timing chain work — making this a very expensive repair if done as a standalone job.
before.solution: Replace internal water pump (GM 12629988 or ACDelco 251-749). Best practice: replace water pump and all three timing chain sets simultaneously since the timing cover must be removed for both procedures. Combined job: $2,800-5,500. If water pump fails alone, this is the time to do timing chains preemptively if over 80,000 miles.
symptoms: Low coolant level warning with no visible external leak
Overheating under load or on hills
White residue in coolant overflow tank

citations.title: GM Bulletin 10246712 - Acadia Water-Pump Shaft Seal

proposal.title: 3.6L V6 Internal Water Pump Failure and Coolant Leak
proposal.description: GM customer-satisfaction bulletin 13079 covers certain 2009-2013 GMC Acadia vehicles with 3.6L High Feature V6 engines (RPO LY7 or LLT) that may experience leakage from the water-pump shaft seal, often after operation with low coolant.

before.title: 3.6L V6 (LGZ) Excessive Oil Consumption from Clogged PCV Orifice
before.description: The 3.6L V6 lacks a serviceable PCV valve and instead uses a fixed PCV orifice and drain-back baffle molded into a valve cover. The orifice and baffle drain hole sludge up and clog, pulling oil into the intake and causing excessive oil consumption (owners report ~1 qt per 1,000 miles). Severe cases foul spark plugs and contaminate the catalytic converters.
before.solution: Verify consumption with GM's oil consumption test. Clean the clogged PCV orifice/baffle drain or replace the affected valve cover with the redesigned part; address underlying blow-by if present. Keep oil changes on schedule and monitor level between services.
symptoms: Low oil level / adding oil between changes
Blue smoke from exhaust on startup or acceleration
Oily residue pooling in the intake resonator/manifold

before.title: 8L45 8-Speed Transmission Torque Converter Shudder
before.description: The 2015+ Canyon with the 3.6L V6 uses the GM 8L45 8-speed automatic (smaller sibling of the 8L90 in full-size trucks) which suffers the same torque converter lock-up clutch shudder at light throttle between 25-50 mph. The clutch friction material degrades and contaminates the fluid. GM issued TSB 18-NA-355 and Customer Satisfaction Program 18302 extending coverage to 6 years/100,000 miles. The fix and fluid are identical to the Sierra 1500 8L90 procedure — Mobil 1 Synthetic LV ATF HP (GM 19417577). This is the same issue affecting the Chevrolet Colorado V6.
before.solution: Full fluid exchange with Mobil 1 Synthetic LV ATF HP (GM 19417577 / Mobil 124715). Check CSP 18302 coverage. Torque converter replacement (GM 24288818 for 8L45) if fluid exchange fails. Full exchange requires 10-12 quarts for the 8L45.
symptoms: Shudder or vibration at light throttle 25-50 mph
Rumble strip sensation at highway cruising
Shudder disappears when throttle is increased

before.title: 2.8L Duramax DEF System Faults and DPF Regeneration Issues
before.description: The 2016+ Canyon Duramax 2.8L LWN diesel uses DEF (Diesel Exhaust Fluid) injection and a DPF (Diesel Particulate Filter) as part of its SCR emissions system. Owners frequently report DEF quality/level sensor faults, DPF regeneration failures in stop-and-go use, DEF pump failures, and NOx sensor faults. Trucks used primarily for short trips often cannot complete DPF regeneration cycles, leading to DPF plugging and the truck going into reduced power mode. GM issued multiple TSBs on DEF sensor calibration and DPF regen procedures.
before.solution: For DPF regeneration issues: take a 20+ minute highway drive at 55+ mph weekly to allow forced regen. For DEF sensor codes: replace DEF quality sensor (GM 84006963). For plugged DPF: forced stationary regeneration at dealer. Keep DEF tank above 1/4 to avoid speed limiter activation. Use only API certified BlueDEF or equivalent.
symptoms: Check engine light with DEF quality codes (P204F, P2BAD, P20EE)
DIC message: DEF Quality Poor - see dealer
Rough idle or loss of power (plugged DPF)
Exhaust smoke during forced DPF regen cycle
Speed limiter engaging below 5 mph when DEF is empty

before.title: Front Suspension Clunk and Stabilizer Bar End Link Failure
before.description: The 2015+ Canyon experiences front end clunking and rattling over bumps and during steering inputs. The most common cause is worn front stabilizer bar end links, though lower control arm ball joints and upper strut mounts also contribute. The end links use a ball-and-socket design that wears quickly on trucks used off-road or in harsh winter road conditions. GM issued TSB PIT5488 for front end noise diagnosis on the Canyon/Colorado platform. The issue is shared with the Chevrolet Colorado, which shares the identical GMSV platform.
before.solution: Replace front stabilizer bar end links (Moog K750744, or OEM GM 23377014). Inspect and replace ball joints if play detected (Moog K500119 lower ball joint). Upper strut mount replacement if clunk is isolated to strut area (GM 84131517). Torque all suspension fasteners to spec — loose bolts cause clunking symptoms.
symptoms: Clunking noise from front suspension over bumps
Rattling at low speed over rough surfaces
Clunk when turning steering wheel at parking lot speeds
Front end noise when rocking the truck side to side
Visible play in end link ball joints

before.title: P0420/P0430 Catalytic Converter Efficiency Failure (3.6L V6)
before.description: On the 3.6L V6 (LGZ) Canyon, the catalytic converters lose efficiency and trigger P0420 (Bank 1) and/or P0430 (Bank 2), often a downstream consequence of the engine's PCV-related oil consumption that contaminates the converter substrate and O2 sensors. before.title: Oil Pressure Sending Unit Failure
before.description: Same oil pressure sensor issue as Chevrolet C/K 1500. The sending unit fails, giving false zero or erratic oil pressure readings. Oil can leak through the electrical connector. Aftermarket sensors have shorter service life. Always verify actual oil pressure with a mechanical gauge before condemning the engine.
before.solution: First, confirm the engine’s true oil pressure with a mechanical test gauge installed at the sender port; if pressure is within spec, the oil pressure sending unit is the likely fault rather than an internal engine problem. Inspect for oil wicking through the sender body or connector, then replace the sender with a quality ACDelco/GM unit and repair the pigtail if it is oil-soaked or brittle; on these trucks the sender is typically near the distributor/rear of the intake manifold on many V8s. Clear any leaked oil from the connector, verify stable gauge operation and no warning light flicker after replacement, and recheck for leaks. Typical cost is about $25-$60 for the sender, $20-$50 for a connector if needed, and roughly 0.5-1.0 hour labor, bringing most shop repairs to about $100-$250.
symptoms: Oil pressure gauge reading zero at idle

before.title: 5.7L Vortec Spider Injector Assembly Failure
before.description: Same CPI spider injector issue as Chevrolet C/K. The 5.7L Vortec V8 spider assembly poppet nozzles clog and fuel lines crack.
before.solution: Confirm the failure by checking fuel pressure and leak-down, then remove the upper intake plenum and inspect the CSFI "spider" for fuel staining, cracked nylon lines, or sticking poppet nozzles at the intake ports. The permanent repair is to replace the original central sequential fuel injection assembly with the updated GM MFI spider conversion kit (commonly GM/ACDelco 12568332 or superseding part), along with the upper plenum gasket and, if needed, the fuel pressure regulator. Parts typically run about $250-$450, and labor is usually 2-4 hours, bringing total repair cost to roughly $500-$900 depending on shop rates.

before.title: Brake Line Corrosion and Rust-Through
before.description: Same brake line corrosion issue as Chevrolet C/K 2500 and all GMT800 trucks. Steel brake lines corrode under securing clips on the frame rail, especially in salt-belt states. NHTSA investigated 6 million GMT800 trucks but no recall was issued. The lines can burst without warning, causing complete brake failure.
before.solution: Inspect all steel brake lines from the master cylinder/ABS module to the frame rails and rear axle, paying close attention to areas hidden by plastic/metal retaining clips and above the fuel tank where rust commonly forms; if any line is heavily scaled, wet, or leaking, replace the entire affected line set rather than patching a single section. The preferred repair is a complete pre-bent stainless or NiCopp brake line kit with new fittings, followed by bleeding the full hydraulic system (including ABS if required by the scan tool/service procedure) and replacing any contaminated hoses or calipers/wheel cylinders found leaking. After repair, flush in fresh DOT 3 brake fluid, secure the new lines with updated clips or protective wrap to reduce future chafing/corrosion, and road-test for pedal firmness and proper ABS operation. Typical cost is about $800-$1,800 for full line replacement depending on rust severity, labor, and whether fuel tank removal or additional brake component replacement is needed.
symptoms: Visible rust and flaking on brake lines

before.solution: Replace the fuel pump module assembly including the sending unit and strainer. Drop the fuel tank for access. Use an OEM or quality aftermarket pump — cheap pumps fail quickly in these trucks.
symptoms: Whining noise from fuel tank area

before.title: Hydroboost Brake Booster Failure and Hard Brake Pedal
before.description: The C/K 3500 diesel models use a hydroboost brake booster (power steering pressure-assisted) rather than a vacuum booster because diesel engines produce insufficient vacuum. The hydroboost unit develops internal seal leaks that cause a hard brake pedal, loss of power steering assist, and power steering fluid leaks. Gas-engine C/K 3500 models can also have hydroboost on heavy-duty configurations. A failed hydroboost creates a very hard brake pedal that requires extreme pedal force to stop the heavy truck.
before.solution: Replace or rebuild the hydroboost unit. Remanufactured units from Cardone (52-7370) are available. Check the power steering pump output pressure and replace if low — a weak pump can cause hydroboost symptoms. Flush the power steering system with new fluid after repair. Check the hydroboost accumulator — it should hold enough pressure for 2-3 power-assisted brake applications with the engine off.
symptoms: Very hard brake pedal requiring excessive force
Loss of power steering assist simultaneously
Power steering fluid leaking from behind brake master cylinder
Groaning noise when pressing brake pedal

before.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Premature Failure
before.description: The C/K 3500 uses an in-tank electric fuel pump that fails prematurely, often at 80,000-120,000 miles. The truck's large fuel tank (up to 42 gallons) means the pump works harder to maintain pressure over a longer fuel column. Running the tank below 1/4 regularly accelerates failure because the fuel cools and lubricates the pump — low fuel means less cooling. The dual-tank models are particularly problematic as the fuel switching valve can fail and starve one pump.
before.solution: Replace the fuel pump assembly (includes pump, strainer, and sending unit). Use an AC Delco or Delphi pump for reliability. On dual-tank models, replace the tank selector valve and check valve at the same time. Replace the fuel filter (external, frame-mounted) during the repair. Consider adding a supplemental fuel pressure gauge to monitor pump health.
symptoms: Engine stalling or dying at idle
Whining noise from fuel tank area
Engine sputtering under load or going uphill
Loss of power at high RPM

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 90V170 - GMC K3500 Seat-Belt Instructions

before.title: Idler Arm and Pitman Arm Premature Wear
before.description: The C/K 3500 with the conventional cab (not crew cab) uses an idler arm and pitman arm steering linkage that wears prematurely under the truck's heavy front axle weight. The idler arm bushing develops free play, causing steering wander and a dead spot at center. The pitman arm splines can also strip at the steering box sector shaft. Large tires and lift kits accelerate wear dramatically. This is one of the most common C/K 3500 front-end complaints.
before.solution: Replace the idler arm and pitman arm together. Use Moog greaseable replacement parts with zerk fittings — the factory sealed parts cannot be re-lubricated and fail faster. Replace the center link (drag link) and tie rod ends at the same time if worn. A front-end alignment is mandatory after replacement. Grease all zerk fittings every oil change.
symptoms: Steering wanders or drifts at highway speeds
Dead spot in steering at center
Front tires wearing on inner or outer edges
Clunking from front end when hitting bumps
Steering wheel not centered while driving straight

before.title: 4.2L I6 Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure and Stalling
before.description: The 4.2L LL8 inline-6 engine in the 2002-2009 GMC Envoy is notorious for crankshaft position sensor failures that cause intermittent stalling and no-start conditions. The sensor is located on the side of the engine block and is exposed to heat soak from the exhaust manifold, accelerating its failure. A failing sensor causes the PCM to lose track of crank position, resulting in the engine cutting out without warning — often at highway speed. The issue tends to be intermittent at first, making diagnosis challenging. Replacement is straightforward and the part is inexpensive.
before.solution: Replace crankshaft position sensor (ACDelco 213-3521 or Delphi SS11378). Clear codes and test. If stalling continues, inspect camshaft position sensor (ACDelco 213-3522) as secondary cause. Verify PCM software is current — older PCM calibrations make the engine overly sensitive to sensor signal dropout.
symptoms: Engine stalls without warning at any speed
Hard start or no-start after hot soak
Check engine light with code P0335 or P0336
Engine cranks but won't fire when hot
Intermittent stall that restarts after cooling down

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 01V126 - Envoy Control-Arm Brackets

before.title: Instrument Cluster Gauge Stepper Motor Failure
before.description: The 2003-2007 GMC Envoy shares the GMT360 platform instrument cluster with the Chevrolet Trailblazer, Buick Rainier, and Oldsmobile Bravada. All gauges (speedometer, tachometer, fuel, temperature, oil pressure, battery voltage) use tiny X27.168 stepper motors that fail from thermal cycling. Gauges read incorrectly, stick, peg at maximum, or go completely dead. The stepper motor failure is the single most reported electrical issue on the Envoy. GM issued Special Coverage 07036 covering some VINs. This is a DIY-repairable issue for those comfortable with basic soldering.
before.solution: Replace all gauge stepper motors simultaneously with X27.168 kit. Professional cluster rebuild services ($150-250). Dorman 599-315 remanufactured cluster (plug-and-play, no programming required). DIY stepper motor kit available for $20-40 — requires cluster removal, disassembly, and soldering.
symptoms: Speedometer pegged at maximum or reads incorrectly
Fuel gauge shows empty when full (or full when empty)
Temperature gauge stuck cold or pegged hot
All gauges sweeping to maximum on startup then dropping to zero

before.title: Transfer Case Encoder Motor and Front Axle Actuator Failure
before.description: The 2002-2009 Envoy uses the BorgWarner 4482 (Auto-Trak) transfer case with an electric encoder motor for 4WD engagement. The encoder motor and its associated hall-effect position sensor fail regularly between 80,000-120,000 miles, causing 4WD to not engage, 4WD warning lights, and the truck occasionally shifting to neutral while driving. The front axle disconnect actuator also fails, causing a grinding or chirping from the front differential in 2WD mode when the axle doesn't fully disengage. Both issues are well-documented on GMT360 platform vehicles (Trailblazer, Rainier, Bravada).
before.solution: Replace encoder motor (ACDelco D1956A or Dorman 600-900). Replace front axle actuator if grinding present (Dorman 600-115). Change transfer case fluid (ACDelco Auto-Trak II, 88900402). Check for corroded wiring harness to encoder motor — a common no-fix-needed finding.
symptoms: 4WD will not engage — light flashes but doesn't solidify
Service 4WD or 4WD Off message on DIC
Grinding or chirping from front axle at highway speed
Transfer case drops to neutral while driving (dangerous)
4WD indicator cycles but no engagement felt

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 01V283 - Envoy Transfer Case

before.title: A-Pillar Water Leak Disables Door Switches
before.description: Water can enter the inside of the upper A-pillar on the driver side due to inadequate sealing, leading to corrosion on the in-line connector (X500) for the driver-side door switches. This causes the door lock, power mirror, and window switches to become inoperative. The issue is particularly problematic because the Hummer EV's removable roof panels may contribute to water channeling into the A-pillar area. GM issued a Technical Service Bulletin addressing the connector corrosion.
before.solution: Have a GMC dealer inspect and reseal the driver-side A-pillar area and replace the corroded X500 in-line connector. The repair involves resealing the A-pillar weatherstripping and replacing the corroded connector terminals ($200-$500 at dealer). If door switches are intermittent, check for moisture in the A-pillar before replacing the switch pack itself. Apply dielectric grease to the connector after repair to prevent future corrosion.
symptoms: Door lock switch becomes intermittent or inoperative
Visible moisture or water stains inside the A-pillar trim
Switches work intermittently, especially after rain or car wash

before.title: Battery Pack Enclosure Water Ingress
before.description: The high-voltage battery pack enclosure on certain 2022-2023 GMC Hummer EV Pickups may not be properly sealed due to flanges that were not properly primed or electrocoated, inhibiting adhesion of the urethane sealant. Water can enter the battery pack, potentially causing a loss of drive power. GM confirmed at least three incidents including one at their proving grounds where the vehicle lost propulsion while driving. NHTSA Recall 22V-771 covers approximately 735 affected vehicles.
before.solution: Contact your GMC dealer immediately to have the battery pack enclosure inspected and resealed under NHTSA Recall 22V-771 at no cost. The dealer will inspect the battery pack sealing and apply proper primer and sealant as needed. Do not drive through deep water or heavy flooding until the recall is completed. If the vehicle will not start or loses power, have it towed to the dealer rather than attempting to drive it.
symptoms: Vehicle will not start after exposure to rain or water
Service High Voltage System warning message
Multiple warning lights on dashboard simultaneously
Reduced range or charging anomalies after wet conditions

before.title: Public Charging Failures and Software Anomalies
before.description: Some GMC Hummer EV models experience a software anomaly that prevents the vehicle from initiating the charge sequence when plugged into public DC fast chargers. The issue may be caused by oversized or damaged terminals in the charge cord connector at frequently-used stations, but a software bug also prevents the vehicle from gracefully handling connection errors. Additionally, the battery energy control module may fail to exit its commissioning (start-up) state due to the cell monitoring unit going offline, requiring a dealer software reprogram of both the battery energy control module and drive motor control module.
before.solution: Visit a GMC dealer for the latest battery energy control module and drive motor control module software updates. If charging fails at a public station, try a different charger or use Level 2 AC charging as a workaround. For the commissioning state issue, a dealer reprogram of the BECM and DMCM is required. GM has released multiple software updates addressing these issues — ensure your vehicle has the latest calibration files installed.
symptoms: Vehicle fails to initiate charging at DC fast chargers
Charging session starts but immediately stops
Service High Voltage System warning appears
Vehicle enters reduced power or limp mode
One Pedal Driving Unavailable warning message

before.title: Adaptive Air Suspension Calibration Errors and Extract Mode Failures
before.description: The Hummer EV SUV's adaptive air suspension system, which offers up to 16 inches of ground clearance in Extract Mode, can develop calibration errors that prevent the system from reaching full height. The height sensors, air compressor, and air springs must all function in concert. Software bugs can cause the system to display incorrect ride height or refuse to enter Extract Mode. The compressor can also overheat from repeated height adjustment cycles, entering a cooldown period that locks out suspension adjustments.
before.solution: GM has released software updates that improve air suspension calibration accuracy. Visit the dealer for recalibration using the GDS2 diagnostic tool. If the compressor overheats, allow it to cool for 30 minutes before attempting further adjustments. For persistent Extract Mode failures, the height sensors may need recalibration or replacement.
symptoms: Extract Mode not reaching full height
Compressor cooldown message after multiple height changes

before.title: DC Fast Charging Speed Reduction and Charge Port Issues
before.description: Some Hummer EV SUVs experience slower-than-expected DC fast charging speeds and intermittent charge port communication failures. The vehicle's 800V architecture should support 350 kW charging, but software limitations and battery temperature management can reduce speeds significantly. The charge port door actuator can also fail, preventing the port from opening. CCS connector fit issues at some public charging stations cause the vehicle to reject the charge session.
before.solution: Pre-condition the battery for DC fast charging by enabling the "target charge station" feature in navigation — this warms the battery to optimal temperature before arrival. Ensure the latest OTA software update is installed, as GM has improved charging algorithms. For charge port door issues, the actuator can be replaced under warranty. Try multiple charger brands if one consistently fails to connect.
symptoms: DC fast charging capping at 100-150 kW instead of 350 kW
Unable to initiate charging at some stations
Battery preconditioning not activating before arrival at charger

before.title: Multiple Warning Lights with Speed Limited to 36 MPH

The dealer will perform a full module scan and reprogram affected control units. Multiple visits may be required as GM releases updated software calibrations.
symptoms: Multiple warning messages appear on the dashboard simultaneously
Vehicle speed limited to approximately 36 mph
CrabWalk and four-wheel steering features disabled

before.title: Lower Ball Joint Failure
before.description: Same ball joint issue as S-10/Blazer. Lower ball joints wear prematurely, especially on 4WD models, and can separate.
before.solution: Inspect the front suspension with the vehicle safely lifted and the lower control arm supported, then check the lower ball joints for vertical/horizontal play using a pry bar and dial indicator or by unloading the joint per GM service procedure; also inspect the upper ball joints, idler arm, tie rods, and front tires because wear often occurs together. If any looseness exceeds spec or the boot is torn/dry, replace the lower ball joints on both sides; on 4WD models this typically requires removing the steering knuckle and pressing the joints out/in with a ball-joint press, followed by greasing serviceable replacements and performing a full front-end alignment. If the control arm bore is damaged or corrosion is severe, replace the control arm assembly instead of only the joint. Typical repair cost is about $400-$900 for both lower ball joints with alignment, depending on 2WD/4WD configuration and whether additional front-end parts are worn.

before.title: 4.3L V6 Intake Manifold Gasket Leak
before.description: Same intake gasket issue as the Astro van. The under-dash engine location makes this a more labor-intensive repair.
before.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the lower intake manifold gasket area for external coolant seepage or signs of internal leakage such as unexplained coolant loss, milky oil, or cylinder misfire; on the 4.3L V6, the original plastic/rubber gasket design is a common failure point. Repair requires removing the upper plenum and lower intake manifold, cleaning the sealing surfaces, and installing the updated lower intake manifold gasket set with new bolts if specified, then refilling and properly bleeding the cooling system and changing the oil if coolant contamination occurred. Because the Safari’s doghouse engine access makes labor tighter than many trucks, this job typically runs about 6-9 labor hours, with total repair costs commonly around $700-$1,300 depending on shop rate and whether related items like hoses, thermostat, or distributor components are replaced at the same time.

before.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Failure
before.description: Common fuel pump failure. The Safari twin-tank models have additional complexity with the tank switching system.
before.solution: Confirm low fuel pressure at the rail with a gauge before replacing parts; the 4.3L V6 should typically show pressure in the mid-50 to low-60 psi range, and a weak pump often causes hard starting, stalling, or loss of power under load. Check the fuel pump relay, fuse, wiring at the tank connector, and on twin-tank models inspect the tank selector/switching valve and related wiring because a fault there can mimic a bad pump. If pressure is low and power/ground are present at the pump, replace the in-tank fuel pump module and strainer, and strongly consider replacing the fuel filter and corroded connector pigtail at the same time; labor usually requires dropping the tank, with typical total repair cost around $500-$1,000 depending on tank configuration and rust. After installation, verify prime pressure, running pressure, and proper tank switching operation on dual-tank systems.

before.title: Brake Line Corrosion and Brake Fluid Loss (Rust Belt)
before.description: The 2003-2014 GMC Savana uses steel brake lines that are subject to severe corrosion in salt-belt states. The factory lines corrode from the outside in and can rupture without warning, causing catastrophic brake failure. This is the same safety-critical issue as documented across all GM full-size truck/van platforms of the same era. Commercial Savanas that operate year-round in Northern states, where road salt is used heavily, are at highest risk. NHTSA has received hundreds of complaints on brake line corrosion leading to loss of braking ability.
before.solution: Inspect all brake lines annually in rust-belt states. Replace corroded lines with Dorman stainless steel pre-bent replacement sets. Consider full brake line replacement as preventive maintenance at 100,000+ miles on any Savana that has lived in salt-belt states.
symptoms: Brake fluid level dropping with no external wheel leak
Visible rust or corrosion on brake lines under vehicle
Complete loss of braking after line rupture

before.title: Fuel Pump Module Failure and Hard Start / Stalling
before.description: The GMC Savana (and Chevrolet Express) fuel pump module is known for premature failure between 80,000-140,000 miles, often stranding drivers without warning. The in-tank electric fuel pump motor burns out or the sending unit becomes erratic. Running the tank consistently below 1/4 generates heat that shortens pump life. Commercial use Savanas that frequently run low on fuel — common in fleet operations — see pump failures well before 80,000 miles. The fuel pump is a demanding repair requiring tank removal on the Savana.
before.solution: Replace fuel pump module (ACDelco MU1374 for 6.0L Savana, MU1373 for 4.8L). Keep fuel tank above 1/4 full at all times. For fleet vehicles, replace pump proactively at 100,000 miles. Aftermarket Walbro or Delphi pumps are common alternatives.
symptoms: Hard start or extended cranking before engine fires
Engine stalls at idle and won't restart when hot
Fuel pressure below specification (should be 55-60 psi)
Engine stumbles and hesitates under load
No-start condition with no fuel pressure
Fuel gauge erratic or reads wrong

before.description: P0011 means the Bank 1 intake camshaft is timed more advanced than the ECM commanded — the phaser is stuck/biased advanced. On the Sierra 1500 5.3L/6.2L, the dominant cause is a VVT (camshaft actuator) solenoid whose internal screen has clogged with oil sludge or AFM debris, jamming the plunger so oil pressure to the phaser can't be modulated. GM acknowledges sticking/binding solenoids in PIs such as PIP5130K and PIP5855. Low or incorrect-viscosity oil is a very common trigger, so oil condition is always checked first. Because AFM lifter wear sheds metal into the oil, that debris circulates and clogs the solenoid screens — tying P0011 directly to the trucks' oil-consumption reputation. Drivers report rough running, and in worse cases stalling when slowing to a stop.
before.solution: Check engine oil level, viscosity, and condition first; an oil/filter change with correct-spec oil sometimes clears it. A proven test is swapping the Bank 1 intake solenoid with another solenoid — if the code follows to P0014/P0021, the solenoid is bad. Replace the VVT/cam actuator solenoid (roughly $40-$90 part). If the phaser or timing chain is worn, the timing set must be replaced.
symptoms: Stalling when slowing to a stop

before.title: P0016 — Crank/Cam Correlation Fault from Stretched Timing Chain on 5.3L AFM V8
before.description: P0016 means the crankshaft and Bank 1 intake camshaft are out of sync beyond tolerance. On the 5.3L V8 Sierra 1500 this is a signature failure because of two engine-specific problems: (1) the timing chain stretches over time — accelerated by AFM lifter debris and extended oil-change intervals — retarding cam timing until correlation exceeds threshold; and (2) the cam actuator (VVT) solenoid or phaser sticks. The AFM V8s are also known for oil consumption, and low/dirty oil starves the phasers and clogs solenoid screens, which both triggers P0016 and worsens chain wear. This is more serious than the related P0011: a severely stretched chain can jump a tooth and cause piston-to-valve contact, so continued driving is risky.
before.solution: Check oil level/condition first — low or sludged oil alone can set it. Use a scan tool to read cam-retard/phaser data. If the timing chain is stretched (confirmed by measuring cam retard or valve-cover inspection), replace the timing chain, guides, tensioner, and cam phaser/sprocket; if only the VVT solenoid is stuck, replace it. Address AFM oil consumption to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Rattle from front of engine on cold start
Hard start or stalling in severe cases

before.title: P0128 — Engine Never Reaches Operating Temp from a Stuck-Open Thermostat
before.description: On the Sierra 1500, P0128 means the coolant did not reach the expected regulating temperature within the time/airflow the ECM predicted — almost always a thermostat stuck open (or partly open) so the engine runs too cool. The GM thermostat on the 5.3L/6.2L is integrated into a plastic housing on the engine, and the common failure is the thermostat losing its ability to close, letting coolant circulate continuously. Drivers notice the temp gauge sitting low, weak or slow-to-warm cabin heat (especially in winter), and worse fuel economy because the ECM stays in open-loop enrichment longer. A stuck-open thermostat is by far the most frequent cause; a failed/biased coolant temperature sensor is the secondary suspect and should be verified with live data before parts are thrown at it.
before.solution: Verify actual coolant temperature with a scan tool vs. the gauge to separate a bad ECT sensor from a bad thermostat. If the engine won't reach ~195-210°F, replace the thermostat (and housing/gasket, commonly sold as an assembly) with an OEM-spec unit and refill/bleed the cooling system. Replace the ECT sensor if data shows an implausible reading.
symptoms: Temp gauge reads low / below normal

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 11V007 - Rear-Axle Cross-Pin Recall

before.title: P0420 — Catalyst Efficiency Bank 1 from Failing Cat, Often Caused by AFM Oil Consumption or Air-Box Debris
before.description: On the 5.3L V8 Sierra 1500, P0420 sets when the downstream (post-cat) O2 sensor tracks the upstream sensor too closely, meaning the Bank 1 catalytic converter is no longer scrubbing exhaust efficiently. The distinctive part on these trucks: the converter frequently dies prematurely from an upstream cause rather than age. Active Fuel Management (AFM) V8s burn oil past the lifters/rings, and that oil ash slowly poisons the catalyst substrate. GM TSB #16-NA-111 also documents a lesser-known trigger: a poor air-filter-housing seal lets abrasive dirt bypass the filter, wearing the O2 sensors and clogging the cat from the inside. Broken exhaust manifold bolts (a chronic GM V8 issue) create leaks that mimic P0420. Aftermarket cats have a poor track record here and often re-trigger the code within months.
before.solution: Do not blindly replace the converter. First scan for exhaust leaks (check manifold bolts), inspect the air-filter housing per TSB 16-NA-111, and check upstream/downstream O2 sensor operation with live data. Address AFM oil consumption if present. If the converter is genuinely spent, install an OEM or high-quality direct-fit unit and complete the heat-cycle break-in before the monitor re-runs.
symptoms: No obvious drivability change in early stages

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 14V007 - Overheated Exhaust Components Recall

before.title: P0430 — Catalyst Efficiency Bank 2 (Driver-Side) Converter Failure on 5.3L V8
before.description: P0430 is the Bank 2 counterpart to P0420 and, on the Sierra 1500 V8, points to the driver-side (Bank 2) catalytic converter falling below efficiency threshold. The mechanism is identical to Bank 1: the rear O2 sensor voltage begins mirroring the front sensor, so the ECM concludes that bank's cat can no longer store/release oxygen. The specific pattern on these trucks is that the underlying killer is usually AFM-related oil consumption or a lazy/aged rear O2 sensor rather than a defective converter out of the box. Owners commonly report P0430 (or both P0420 and P0430) returning even after installing new aftermarket converters — a well-documented frustration on GM-Trucks and SilveradoSierra forums — because the root cause (oil burning, exhaust leak, or a slow O2 sensor) was never corrected.
before.solution: Confirm with a smoke/leak check and O2 sensor live-data (rear sensor should be lazy/flat, not switching). Rule out driver-side manifold bolt leaks. Replace a lazy Bank 2 rear O2 sensor first if indicated. If the converter is confirmed inefficient, fit an OEM/CARB-compliant direct-fit unit and fix any oil consumption; expect aftermarket cats to re-trigger if the AFM oil burn persists.
symptoms: Code returns after aftermarket cat replacement

before.title: P0442 — Small EVAP Leak from Loose/Cracked Gas Cap or Fractured Filler Vent Hose
before.description: P0442 on the Sierra 1500 is a small EVAP leak detected during the ECM's key-off/idle vacuum test. On these trucks the two most common real-world causes are a loose, worn, or cracked gas cap seal (the cheapest fix and always the first check) and — a documented GM issue (TSB 15-NA-019) — the fuel tank filler vent hose connector cracking, which allows vapor to escape and sets P0442 (and sometimes P0455). The vent hose fracture is addressed by replacing the vent hose assembly (part No. 22802073 on 2013-2015 models). The EVAP purge valve (engine bay) and vent solenoid (near the tank) can also weep. Drivers often notice a faint fuel odor and the CEL, with no drivability change.
before.solution: Start with the gas cap — inspect the seal and tighten/replace with OEM. If the code persists, perform a smoke test to pinpoint the leak; inspect the fuel filler vent hose connector for cracks and replace the vent hose assembly if fractured. Replace the purge or vent solenoid if the smoke test isolates it there.

before.title: P0455 — Gross EVAP Leak from Failed Vent Solenoid, Missing Gas Cap, or Broken Vent Hose
before.description: P0455 indicates a large (gross) EVAP leak — the ECM cannot pull or hold vacuum in the evaporative system at all. On the Sierra 1500 the classic causes are a completely missing/unsealed gas cap, a stuck-open or failed EVAP vent solenoid (mounted under the truck near the fuel tank/spare tire, where it's exposed to road spray, dirt, and corrosion), and a cracked or disconnected vapor/vent hose. Because the vent solenoid sits at the canister under the bed, water intrusion and corrosion cause it to stick open, which the ECM reads as a wide-open system; a tell-tale symptom is the fuel nozzle repeatedly clicking off during refueling. The filler vent hose connector fracture noted in GM literature can also escalate to P0455. Symptom-wise the driver usually sees only the CEL, sometimes a fuel smell, and no performance loss.
before.solution: Confirm the gas cap is present and sealing. Smoke-test the EVAP system to find the large leak. The most common repair on these trucks is replacing the under-body EVAP vent solenoid/valve at the canister; also inspect and replace cracked vapor lines and the fuel filler vent hose. Clear codes and run the EVAP monitor to confirm.
symptoms: Fuel nozzle clicks off repeatedly when refueling

before.title: P0700 — Transmission Fault Flag from Failing 6L80/6L90 Internal TEHCM
before.description: P0700 itself is only a flag: the Transmission Control Module has stored one or more transmission faults and is requesting the MIL. On Sierra 1500s with the 6L80 (and 6L90 on heavier variants) 6-speed automatic, the notable design issue is that the TCM is integrated into the valve body as a TEHCM (transmission electro-hydraulic control module), bolted inside the pan and sitting in 180-250°F fluid. Repeated heat cycling degrades the module and its integrated pressure switches and solenoids. When the TEHCM or a shift/pressure-control solenoid begins to fail, it sets specific sub-codes (e.g., P2534, P0742, P0761) plus the umbrella P0700, and the truck can exhibit harsh or missed shifts, slipping, or limp mode. Critically, on the 6L80/6L90 the solenoids are over-molded into the non-serviceable TEHCM and generally can't be replaced individually.
before.solution: P0700 alone is not actionable — pull the transmission-specific sub-codes with a capable scanner to find the real fault. Check fluid level/condition first. Repairs commonly involve replacing the TEHCM/valve body assembly (solenoids are integrated and non-serviceable) and re-learning shift adaptives; the new TEHCM must be programmed to the VIN. Address any fluid overheating cause to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Check engine light with transmission sub-codes

before.title: Allison 1000/2000 Series Transmission Torque Converter Shudder
before.description: The Allison 1000 and 2000 series automatic transmissions paired with Duramax engines in the Sierra 3500HD exhibit torque converter clutch shudder during light throttle cruising between 40–65 MPH as the TCC applies and releases. This is caused by degraded transmission fluid, worn TCC friction material, or contamination in the hydraulic circuit. GM and Allison have acknowledged this issue through multiple fluid specification updates and TSB 07-07-30-022.
before.solution: Drain and refill with Allison-approved TES-295 or TES-468 fluid (Transynd or equivalent); do not use generic ATF. If shudder persists after fluid service, a complete torque converter replacement (remanufactured unit $400–$800) and valve body cleaning is required. GM TSB 07-07-30-022 outlines the fluid change procedure and updated fill volume specifications. Complete transmission fluid flush recommended every 50,000 miles for prevention.
symptoms: Vibration or shudder between 40–65 MPH at light throttle
Shudder disappears under hard acceleration or deceleration
Transmission hesitation or clunk when TCC engages
Rough or inconsistent lockup feel during highway cruising
Transmission fluid with burnt smell or dark discoloration

before.title: Dashboard Instrument Cluster Pixel and Display Failure
before.description: The instrument cluster in 2015-2020 Sierra 3500HD trucks suffers from LCD pixel failure, causing portions of the Driver Information Center (DIC) display to become unreadable. Individual pixels or entire segments go blank, making it impossible to read trip computer data, gear indicator, or warning messages. The issue is caused by solder joint failure on the cluster circuit board from thermal cycling and vibration. The speedometer and tachometer gauges may also develop stepper motor failures, causing inaccurate or stuck readings.
before.solution: The cluster can be sent to a repair service specializing in GM instrument clusters ($150-$300) for re-soldering and stepper motor replacement — this fixes 90% of cases. A new OEM cluster from the dealer costs $500-$1,000 and requires VIN programming. Aftermarket rebuilt clusters are available for $200-$400. Some owners have successfully repaired the solder joints themselves with a soldering iron, but this requires electronics experience. The cluster must be programmed to the truck VIN after replacement.
symptoms: Missing pixels or blank segments on dashboard display
DIC screen partially or fully blank
Gear indicator not showing current gear
Gauges sticking or not returning to zero when off

before.title: Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) System Failures
before.description: The Duramax diesel Sierra 3500HD (2011+) equipped with the DEF/SCR emission system develops failures in the DEF tank heater, DEF quality sensor, and associated wiring. Wires to the DEF tank short out, and because they share a harness with the transmission, this can trigger both DEF and transmission warnings simultaneously. Cold weather operation exacerbates DEF system problems as the fluid crystallizes.
before.solution: Scan the SCR/DEF system for stored DTCs and inspect the DEF tank harness where it runs with the transmission wiring, as chafed or shorted wires commonly cause both DEF and transmission warnings at the same time. Test the DEF tank heater, reductant quality/level sensor, and pump module; replace the failed heater or complete DEF tank header/sensor assembly as needed, repair damaged wiring with updated pigtails, clean any crystallized DEF contamination, and confirm proper heater operation and reductant quality readings with a scan tool. In cold-weather cases, verify the tank heater is drawing current and that the fluid lines are not frozen before condemning other components. Typical repair cost ranges from about $300-$800 for harness or heater repairs, and $900-$1,800 if the DEF tank/header assembly must be replaced.
symptoms: Check engine light with SCR-related codes
Transmission warning alongside DEF warning (shared wiring)
DEF system not heating in cold weather

before.title: DPF (Diesel Particulate Filter) Clogging and Regeneration Failure
before.description: The Duramax diesel DPF becomes clogged with soot under low-speed, short-trip, or heavy towing duty cycles that prevent complete passive regeneration. Owners report the truck entering limp mode, reduced power, and repeated active regen cycles that fail to fully clean the filter. GM TSB 14-06-04-003 addresses regen strategy calibration updates for LML and L5P engines.
before.solution: Forced active regen via Tech 2 or MDI scan tool; if clogging is severe, DPF removal and professional cleaning or replacement. Updated ECM calibration per TSB 14-06-04-003. Replacement DPF (ACDelco 84031507 or OEM equivalent) runs $800–$2,500. Extended highway driving after software update can restore function in mild cases.
symptoms: Reduced engine power / limp mode activation
DPF warning light or message on DIC
Frequent or incomplete regen cycles with elevated exhaust temps
Excessive fuel dilution in engine oil
Sulfur or burning smell from exhaust during failed regen

before.title: CP4.2 High-Pressure Fuel Pump Catastrophic Failure
before.description: The Sierra 3500HD Duramax diesel uses the same Bosch CP4.2 high-pressure fuel pump as the 2500HD. The pump is prone to catastrophic failure that destroys the entire fuel injection system (all 6 injectors, fuel rails, return lines). The 3500HD is often used for heavier towing and work applications, which places more sustained load on the high-pressure fuel system and may accelerate CP4.2 wear. Total system replacement costs $10,000-18,000. A CP3 conversion kit (Fleece FPE-CP3K-LML or FPE-CP3K-L5P) is strongly recommended as a preventive upgrade on any high-mileage Sierra 3500HD Duramax.
before.solution: Replace entire fuel system on failure. Preventive CP3 conversion kit (Fleece FPE-CP3K-LML for LML, FPE-CP3K-L5P for L5P). Install FASS lift pump. Never run below 1/4 tank.
symptoms: Loss of power under towing load
Fuel rail pressure codes P0087, P0191

before.title: Duramax Water Pump Failure and Coolant Leak
before.description: The factory water pump on 6.6L Duramax engines (LBZ, LMM, LML, L5P) is known to develop weep hole leaks and bearing failures, resulting in coolant loss and potential overheating. symptoms: Coolant puddle under front center of engine

Engine overheating warning or high coolant temperature
Squealing or grinding noise from front of engine

before.title: Exhaust Manifold Cracking and Warping (Duramax L5P/LML)
before.description: The cast iron exhaust manifolds on the Duramax diesel engine are prone to cracking and warping due to extreme exhaust gas temperatures and thermal cycling. Cracks typically develop at the manifold-to-head mounting points, causing exhaust leaks that produce a ticking noise on cold starts. The up-pipe connections also warp, allowing soot to blow onto engine components. This issue affects both the LML (2015-2016) and L5P (2017-2024) engines.
before.solution: Replace the cracked exhaust manifold with OEM or upgraded aftermarket units ($400-$800 per side for parts). PPE and Pacific Performance Engineering make reinforced stainless steel manifolds ($600-$1,200) that resist cracking. New exhaust manifold bolts and gaskets are essential during replacement — always use OEM bolts as they are designed for the thermal expansion. Labor runs 4-8 hours ($600-$1,200) depending on which side. Inspect up-pipes for warping at the same time.
symptoms: Ticking or tapping noise on cold start that fades as engine warms
Exhaust smell in cab especially at idle
Soot buildup on engine components near manifold
Visible cracks in exhaust manifold on inspection

before.title: Front Differential Actuator Failure Causing 4WD Engagement Problems
before.description: The front axle disconnect actuator (also called the front axle engagement actuator or IWE—Integrated Wheel End) on four-wheel-drive Sierra 3500HD models is known to fail, preventing proper engagement or disengagement of 4WD. Labor 1–3 hours depending on configuration.

Service 4WD warning message on instrument cluster
Front axle vibration at highway speeds

before.title: Diesel Injector Failure Causing White Smoke and Rough Running
before.description: The Bosch piezoelectric fuel injectors on the Duramax L5P and LML engines can fail due to contaminated fuel, high-mileage wear, or internal electrical faults. A failed injector causes white smoke on startup, rough idle, misfires on the affected cylinder, and fuel dilution of the engine oil. The high fuel rail pressures (up to 36,000 PSI on the L5P) stress the injectors over time. Contaminated fuel from bulk diesel stations accelerates injector wear.
before.solution: Diagnose the failed injector with a relative compression test and injector balance rate scan using a Tech 2 or equivalent scan tool. Replace the failed injector(s) — OEM Bosch injectors are $300-$500 each, and labor is 2-4 hours per injector ($300-$600). Always replace the injector hold-down clamp and fuel return line seals. If one injector fails at high mileage, consider replacing all 8 as the others are likely near end of life. Use a quality fuel additive like Stanadyne or Hot Shot Secret to protect remaining injectors.
symptoms: White or gray smoke on cold start
Rough idle or misfire on one or more cylinders
Fuel smell in engine oil (fuel dilution)
Check engine light with injector circuit codes
Reduced power and poor fuel economy

before.title: Rear Leaf Spring Breakage Under Heavy Loads
before.description: The rear leaf spring packs on the Sierra 3500HD are prone to breaking or cracking under sustained heavy loads, particularly when used for frequent towing, hauling, or with fifth-wheel hitches. The main leaf or secondary leaves fracture at the spring eye or center bolt area. Broken springs cause the truck to sag on one side, produce clunking noises over bumps, and can damage brake lines or fuel lines if a broken leaf shifts.
before.solution: Replace the broken leaf spring pack — OEM replacement packs run $300-$600 per side plus 2-4 hours labor. For trucks that regularly tow or haul near capacity, upgrade to heavy-duty aftermarket leaf springs from Deaver or National Spring ($500-$900 per side) or add supplemental air bags ($200-$500) to reduce spring stress. Torque the U-bolts to spec and inspect spring bushings during replacement. Consider adding a helper spring or overload spring for frequent heavy towing.
symptoms: Truck sagging on one side when loaded
Clunking or banging noise from rear over bumps
Visible crack or break in leaf spring
Rear axle shifted to one side
Uneven tire wear on rear axle
Poor ride quality and excessive bouncing when empty

before.title: Rear axle pinion seal leak and differential fluid loss (AAM 11.5/11.8)
before.description: Owners report gear oil leaks at the rear differential pinion seal, sometimes after towing or sustained highway speeds. NHTSA complaints and owner reports describe oil slinging onto the underbody and a developing howl if fluid level drops. The issue is commonly associated with seal wear, yoke surface wear, or excessive pinion angle/driveline vibration.
before.solution: Confirm leak source (pinion seal vs cover vs axle seals) and check vent operation. Replace the pinion seal and inspect/replace the yoke if grooved; refill with the correct gear oil and additive requirements per axle RPO. If noise persists, inspect bearings and gear pattern for damage from low fluid.
symptoms: Gear oil leak at pinion/yoke area
Burning gear oil smell after towing

before.title: Silverado/Sierra 3500HD Frame Corrosion and Rust-Through (Salt Belt)
before.description: The fully boxed steel frame on 2007–2019 Sierra 3500HD trucks operating in northern and salt-belt states is susceptible to severe corrosion, particularly around crossmember mounting points, rear spring hanger brackets, and fuel/brake line routing areas. NHTSA received numerous complaints (NHTSA ID: 10123456 series) and GM issued extended corrosion warranty coverage in certain regions. Frame rust-through can compromise structural integrity and towing safety.
before.solution: Frame inspection and cleaning, application of rust inhibitor (Fluid Film, Corroseal), or frame section replacement in severe cases. GM extended the corrosion perforation warranty to 6 years/100,000 miles in affected states. Professional rustproofing and annual undercoating application is recommended preventatively. Severe cases may require certified frame repair or vehicle replacement.
symptoms: Visible rust perforation or holes in frame rails or crossmembers
Flaking or bubbling paint on frame underside
Squeaking or creaking from chassis under load
Brake or fuel lines showing external corrosion or leaks
Loose or corroded spring hanger bolts

before.title: Steering Gear Box Leak and Excessive Play
before.description: The recirculating ball steering gear box on the Sierra 3500HD develops fluid leaks at the input shaft seal and sector shaft seal, leading to power steering fluid loss and increased steering play. The heavy-duty application and large tires accelerate wear on the steering box internals. Owners report the steering develops excessive play (1-2 inches at the wheel) and a wandering feeling on the highway, especially when towing.
before.solution: For minor leaks, replace the seals ($50-$100 parts, $300-$500 labor) as a temporary fix. For excessive play, the steering gear box needs replacement with a remanufactured or new unit ($400-$900 for the box). A Borgeson steering box upgrade ($500-$700) is a popular heavy-duty replacement that provides tighter steering and better durability. Always replace the Pitman arm and check tie rod ends during the job. A full front-end alignment is required afterward.
symptoms: Power steering fluid leaking from steering gear box area
Excessive steering wheel play (more than 1 inch)
Wandering on highway requiring constant correction
Groaning or whining from steering when turning
Loose or vague steering feel especially when towing

before.description: On 4WD Sierra 3500HD models with GM transfer cases that use an internal pump, owners report a leak caused by the pump wearing through the magnesium case (commonly called "pump rub"). before.solution: Inspect for transfer case fluid seepage and verify fluid level/condition. If run low, rebuild or replace the transfer case assembly due to chain/bearing damage.
symptoms: Transfer case fluid leak (often rear half)
Whine/grind from transfer case under load
4WD engagement issues or popping out of 4WD
Burnt or low transfer case fluid

before.title: Turbocharger VGT Vane Sticking and Boost Control Failure (Duramax LML/L5P)
before.description: The variable geometry turbocharger (Garrett GT3788VA on LML, and similar VGT on L5P) used on 6.6L Duramax engines develops carbon buildup on the variable vanes, causing them to stick and resulting in loss of boost control. Owners report surging, lack of power under load, black smoke, and check engine lights. This is a widely documented issue in Duramax owner communities and referenced in multiple TSBs including 16-NA-026.
before.solution: Turbocharger vane cleaning using BG Induction Service or equivalent upper-cylinder cleaner introduced through intake. Severe cases require turbo removal and manual vane cleaning or actuator replacement. Complete turbo replacement with remanufactured Garrett unit ($1,200–$2,500 part) is recommended if vanes are seized. Updated VGT actuator calibration via ECM flash per TSB 16-NA-026.
symptoms: Reduced power or hesitation under load, especially above 2000 RPM
Excessive black smoke from exhaust under acceleration
Boost pressure gauge reading lower than normal
Check engine light with boost-related codes

before.title: AFM/DFM Lifter Collapse and Failure
before.description: The Active Fuel Management (AFM) and Dynamic Fuel Management (DFM) systems use special hydraulic lifters that collapse to deactivate cylinders for fuel economy. These lifters are prone to premature failure due to poor physical design and inadequate oil flow. Failures can occur as early as 4-digit mileage on newer trucks or 50,000-100,000 miles on older models. When a lifter fails, it can cause catastrophic engine damage requiring complete engine teardown.
before.solution: Replace all 16 lifters and associated components (camshaft inspection recommended). Install AFM/DFM delete kit to disable cylinder deactivation permanently. Use AFM/DFM disabler device to prevent system activation. Use high-quality synthetic oil and change at 5,000 mile intervals.
symptoms: Check engine light with cylinder misfire codes
Ticking or knocking noise from engine

before.title: Allison 1000/2000 Transmission TCM Failure and Harsh Shifting
before.description: The Allison 1000 (gas) and Allison 2000 (diesel) 6-speed automatic transmissions used in Sierra 2500HD/3500HD are widely regarded as extremely durable, but the Transmission Control Module (TCM) and solenoid pack do develop faults. Common issues include harsh 1-2 shifts, transmission sticking in one gear, slip codes, and the truck going into limp mode (3rd gear only). The Allison's proprietary Transynd fluid is critical — using non-approved fluid is the leading cause of premature solenoid wear. TCM software updates from GM address most calibration-related shift complaints.
before.solution: TCM software update at dealer. Allison Transynd fluid service (drain/fill every 30k miles, full exchange every 60k). Solenoid pack replacement (Allison 29539579). TCM replacement if software update fails. Always use genuine Allison Transynd TES-295 or Mobil Delvac 1 ATF — not GM DEXRON products.
symptoms: Delayed engagement from Park to Drive
Check engine light with transmission codes (P0700, P0730, P0751)
Transmission not shifting above 3rd gear under load

before.title: CP4.2 High-Pressure Fuel Pump Catastrophic Failure
before.description: The Bosch CP4.2 high-pressure fuel injection pump used on the 2011-2016 LML and 2017-2020 L5P Duramax diesel engines is prone to catastrophic failure that destroys the entire fuel injection system. Unlike its predecessor the CP3, the CP4.2 lacks a roller element and relies solely on fuel for lubrication. When metal fatigue occurs, the pump shatters and sends metal debris throughout the entire high-pressure fuel system — contaminating all six injectors, the fuel rails, return lines, and feed lines. Total repair cost runs $8,000-18,000. A class action lawsuit was filed against GM. The same pump also fails in Ford 6.7 Power Stroke and Ram 6.7 Cummins of the same era.
before.solution: Replace entire high-pressure fuel system: CP4 pump, all 6 injectors, both fuel rails, return lines, and flush the lift pump/FASS system. Install aftermarket CP3 conversion kit (Fleece FPE-CP3K-LML or FPE-CP3K-L5P) to replace the CP4.2 with the more durable CP3 design. Add a FASS or AirDog lift pump to improve fuel supply. Prevention: never run below 1/4 tank, use quality diesel fuel.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power under load
Rough running or misfiring on multiple cylinders
Metal shavings or debris visible in fuel filter
White or black smoke from exhaust

before.title: LML Duramax EGR Cooler and EGR Valve Failure
before.description: The LML Duramax EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) cooler is prone to coolant leaks internally, allowing coolant to enter the intake manifold and combustion chambers. Coolant in the intake causes white smoke, rough running, and potential hydrolocking of cylinders. The EGR valve also sticks open or closed from carbon buildup, causing rough idle, black smoke, and check engine lights. The EGR cooler failure can occur as early as 60,000 miles on trucks used in stop-and-go driving. GM issued multiple TSBs addressing EGR cooler design improvements.
before.solution: Replace EGR cooler with updated GM design or aftermarket stainless steel unit (Mishimoto MMEGR-DMAX-LML). Clean or replace EGR valve. Flush cooling system and inspect for coolant contamination in intake. Consider EGR delete kit for off-road/race use only (illegal for street use). Prevent premature failure by maintaining proper coolant pH and avoiding extended idle periods.
symptoms: White smoke from exhaust especially on startup
Coolant loss with no visible external leak
Check engine light with EGR codes (P0401, P0404)
Overheating or coolant in oil (severe cases)
Black smoke and poor fuel economy (EGR valve stuck open)

before.title: Front Axle Disconnect Actuator and IWE Hub Failure (4WD Engagement Issues)
before.description: Sierra 2500HD 4WD trucks use a front axle disconnect system with an electronic actuator and Integrated Wheel End (IWE) hubs. The actuator motor and position sensor commonly fail between 80,000-120,000 miles, causing the 4WD system to not engage, to partially engage (binding and vibration), or to throw a 4WD Service warning. Heavy-duty truck use — particularly towing and off-road — accelerates actuator wear. The IWE hubs (vacuum-operated on some variants, electric on others) also fail, causing a grinding or clicking noise from the front axle in 2WD mode when the hub disengages incompletely.
before.solution: Replace front axle actuator motor (GM 84243791 or Dorman 600-140). Inspect IWE hubs for wear/failure. Change front differential and transfer case fluid simultaneously. Diagnose with scan tool to confirm actuator vs. TCCM fault. Some owners replace vacuum lines on IWE systems with updated silicone lines to prevent cracking.
symptoms: 4WD will not engage or disengages randomly
Service 4WD or Service AWD message on DIC
Grinding or clicking from front axle at highway speed in 2WD
Vibration when 4WD engaged on dry pavement
4WD indicator light flashing or not illuminating

before.title: 6.0L V8 Excessive Oil Consumption and AFM Lifter Wear
before.description: The 6.0L L96 V8 gasoline engine in Sierra 2500HD (non-diesel) suffers from Active Fuel Management (AFM) lifter failures similar to the 5.3L in Sierra 1500 — though less frequently due to the higher displacement. More commonly, 6.0L engines exhibit excessive oil consumption (1 qt per 1,000-3,000 miles) from worn valve stem seals and piston rings, particularly between 100,000-150,000 miles. The L96 is a high-output truck engine subjected to heavy towing and payload, which accelerates wear on AFM components.
before.solution: AFM disabler device (Range Technology RA003B) to prevent lifter wear. Oil consumption: GM oil consumption test procedure — if over 1 qt/2,000 miles, piston ring replacement authorized. Change oil every 5,000 miles with full synthetic Dexos2 5W-30. Valve stem seal replacement for blue smoke on startup.
symptoms: Oil level dropping between changes (check every 1,000 miles)
Blue smoke on cold startup or under heavy acceleration
Spark plug fouling on AFM cylinders
Engine misfire codes P0300, P0301, P0304, P0306, P0307

before.title: Fuel Pump Module Failure Causing No-Start or Stalling

before.solution: Diagnosis usually starts with checking fuel pressure at the rail and verifying pump prime at key-on. Repair is replacement of the complete fuel pump module and, ideally, the fuel filter on applicable years; corroded electrical connectors at the tank should also be inspected and replaced if heat-damaged.

before.title: Knock Sensor Water Intrusion Under Intake Causing Check Engine Light and Reduced Performance

before.title: Rusting Brake Lines Leading to Fluid Loss and Sudden Brake Failure
before.description: Corrosion of steel brake lines is a major safety issue on older Sierra 1500 trucks, especially in salt-belt states. Owners report the brake pedal suddenly dropping to the floor when a rusted line bursts during normal braking, often near the ABS module or along the frame rails. The problem is heavily documented in NHTSA complaints and repair forums for GMT800 trucks and related GM full-size pickups.
before.solution: Inspect all hard brake lines from the master cylinder/ABS module to the rear axle and front calipers, paying close attention to flaking rust and wet spots. Spot repairs may buy time, but many owners end up replacing the full line set with pre-bent stainless or coated steel lines because multiple sections are usually compromised. After replacement, the system must be properly bled, including ABS bleed procedures when needed.
symptoms: brake pedal suddenly goes to floor
visible rust and scaling on brake lines

before.title: Stepper Motor Instrument Cluster Failure Causing Inaccurate Gauges
before.description: 2003-2007 Classic-era Sierra trucks are well known for instrument cluster gauge failures caused by defective stepper motors and, in some cases, backlighting issues. Speedometer, tachometer, oil pressure, fuel, voltage, and coolant gauges can stick, read wildly high or low, or stop moving entirely. The problem became widespread enough that GM issued a special coverage adjustment on many trucks and SUVs using the same cluster design.
before.solution: Verify actual vehicle data with a scan tool or GPS speed app to confirm the cluster is inaccurate rather than the sending unit. Repair is typically cluster removal and professional rebuild with updated stepper motors and bulbs, or replacement with a remanufactured unit programmed for the vehicle. If only one gauge is wrong, the whole cluster is still usually rebuilt because the remaining motors often fail later.
symptoms: speedometer reads 0 or pegs past 120 mph
oil pressure gauge stuck high or low
warning chimes with incorrect gauge readings

before.title: 4.3L V6 Intake Manifold Gasket Leak
before.description: Same intake gasket issue as the S-10 platform. The 4.3L Vortec V6 intake gaskets fail from heat cycling.
before.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the intake manifold-to-head sealing area for external coolant seepage; on the 4.3L Vortec, leaks commonly occur at the lower intake manifold gaskets and can also show up as unexplained coolant loss or overheating. Repair requires removing the upper plenum and lower intake manifold, cleaning the sealing surfaces, and installing the updated metal/rubber intake manifold gasket set with new bolts if specified, then refilling and properly bleeding the cooling system; many technicians also change the thermostat and coolant during the job. If coolant contamination is found in the oil, change the oil and filter immediately after repair. Typical repair cost is about $700-$1,300 depending on labor rates and whether related items like hoses, thermostat, or distributor components are replaced.

before.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Failure
before.description: Same fuel pump failure issues as the S-10. The in-tank pump fails from heat and debris.
before.solution: Confirm low fuel pressure before replacing parts by checking pressure at the Schrader valve on the fuel rail; CPI/Vortec-equipped 4.3L trucks are especially sensitive and typically need about 60-66 psi to start and run correctly, while weak pressure, intermittent drop-out, or excessive current draw points to a failing in-tank pump. Inspect the fuel pump relay, fuse, ground at the frame, and the pump electrical connector for heat damage, then replace the complete in-tank fuel pump module/strainer and install a new fuel filter at the same time; on many Sonomas the tank must be lowered, though removing the bed can also improve access on some configurations. Use a quality Delco or Delphi module rather than a pump-only repair, and clean out any tank debris to prevent repeat failure. Typical repair cost is about $450-$900 parts and labor depending on engine, cab/bed configuration, and whether the sending unit harness also needs replacement.

before.title: 5.7L Vortec Intake Manifold Gasket and CPI Issues
before.description: The GMC Suburban shares the same 5.7L Vortec intake gasket and spider injector issues as the C/K 1500. The larger vehicle runs hotter, which can accelerate gasket degradation.
before.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect for external seepage at the lower intake manifold gasket, then scan fuel trims/misfire data and remove the upper plenum to check the Central Port Injection (CPI) spider for fuel leakage or sticking poppets. Repair typically involves replacing the lower intake manifold gaskets with the updated metal/rubber design, changing coolant and engine oil if contaminated, and torquing the intake in sequence to spec; if the CPI unit is leaking or causing hard starts/rough idle, replace it with the updated MFI spider assembly. Parts are usually about $120-$250 for intake gasket sets and $250-$450 for the injector assembly, with total repair costs commonly running $900-$1,800 depending on labor rates and whether both problems are addressed together.

before.title: Rear AC Evaporator Core and Line Leaks
before.description: The GMC Suburban (and Chevrolet Suburban/Tahoe/Yukon) with rear AC systems develop leaks in the rear evaporator core and the aluminum rear AC lines that run along the passenger-side frame rail. The lines corrode under the securing straps from road salt and moisture. The rear drain tube also clogs, causing musty odors inside the cabin. Repair is costly because the rear AC system is difficult to access.
before.solution: Confirm the leak by recovering the refrigerant, pulling the system into vacuum, and pressure-testing with dry nitrogen and UV dye or an electronic leak detector at the rear evaporator case and the aluminum lines running along the passenger-side frame rail, especially under the retaining clamps. Replace any corroded rear lines and, if leaking, the rear evaporator core and O-rings, then flush debris, evacuate the system, recharge to factory specification, and clear the rear evaporator drain tube to stop water intrusion and mildew odor. Many owners in rust-belt areas choose a rear A/C line delete or block-off kit if rear cooling is not needed, which is cheaper than full line replacement. Typical cost is about $400-$900 for line repair/delete, or roughly $1,200-$2,000+ if the rear evaporator core and interior trim access labor are required.
symptoms: Musty or mildew smell from rear vents
Visible corrosion on rear AC lines along frame rail
